questions.stem: Kabir's federation is facing a demand from some of its states for much greater freedom, while other states fear that too much freedom will break the country apart. In about 45 words, state the two objectives that a federal system has to serve at the same time.

markingPoints.description: The first objective is to safeguard and promote unity of the country
The second objective is, at the same time, to accommodate regional diversity
Stated that both objectives are to be pursued together, as the dual objectives of a federal system

answerScheme.modelAnswer: A federal system has dual objectives. The first is to safeguard and promote unity of the country. The second, pursued at the same time, is to accommodate regional diversity. A federation that serves only one of them cannot hold together states that differ from one another.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: Ravi is preparing a note on how a federation is arranged. In about 45 words, state how many levels of government a federation has, and explain how the different tiers stand in relation to the same citizens.

markingPoints.description: A federation has two or more levels, or tiers, of government
The different tiers of government govern the same citizens
Each tier has its own jurisdiction in specific matters of legislation, taxation and administration

answerScheme.modelAnswer: A federation has two or more levels, or tiers, of government. The different tiers of government govern the same citizens, but each tier has its own jurisdiction in specific matters of legislation, taxation and administration. So every tier acts on the same people, but within its own field of authority.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: Ila is told that her country has a government for the entire country and also governments for its provinces and states, each with powers of its own. In about 75 words, and in steps, explain what a federal system is, how many levels of government it usually has, what each level does, and to whom each level is answerable.

markingPoints.description: Power is divided between a central authority and various constituent units of the country
A federation usually has two levels of government
One level is the government for the entire country, responsible for a few subjects of common national interest
The other level is the government of provinces or states, which looks after much of the day-to-day administering of its state
Both these levels of governments enjoy their power independent of the other and are separately answerable to the people

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1: A federal system is one in which power is divided between a central authority and various constituent units of the country. Step 2: Usually a federation has two levels of government. Step 3: One is the government for the entire country, responsible for a few subjects of common national interest. Step 4: The other is the government at the level of provinces or states, which looks after much of the day-to-day administering of its state. Step 5: Both these levels enjoy their power independent of the other, and both are separately answerable to the people.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: Nandini is asked to place two countries on a chart. In the first country the central government can pass on orders to the provincial or the local government. In the second country the central government cannot order the state government to do something, and the state government holds powers of its own. In about 75 words, and in steps, name the system each country follows and give the reason from the arrangement of power in each.

markingPoints.description: The first country is unitary, with either one level of government or sub-units subordinate to the central government, which can pass on orders to the provincial or the local government
The second country is federal, with power divided between a central authority and various constituent units of the country
In the federal country the central government cannot order the state government to do something
The state government has powers of its own for which it is not answerable to the central government
In a federation both these governments are separately answerable to the people

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1: The first country follows a unitary system, where either there is only one level of government or the sub-units are subordinate to the central government. Step 2: In it the central government can pass on orders to the provincial or the local government, so the centre directs the units. Step 3: The second country follows a federal system, in which power is divided between a central authority and various constituent units of the country. Step 4: There the central government cannot order the state government to do something. Step 5: The state government has powers of its own for which it is not answerable to the central government, and both these governments are separately answerable to the people.

questions.stem: Neel and Poorvi are both federations, but the share of power held by the central government is not the same in the two. In about 75 words, and in steps, explain why the exact balance of power between the central and the state government is not the same in every federation, and describe what happens when independent States come together on their own to form a bigger unit.

markingPoints.description: The exact balance of power between the central and the state government varies from one federation to another
The balance depends mainly on the historical context in which the federation was formed
There are two kinds of routes through which federations have been formed
The first route involves independent States coming together on their own to form a bigger unit
They do this by pooling their sovereignty and retaining their identity

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1: The exact balance of power between the central and the state government varies from one federation to another. Step 2: This balance depends mainly on the historical context in which the federation was formed, so federations formed in different circumstances share power differently. Step 3: There are two kinds of routes through which federations have been formed. Step 4: In the first route independent States come together on their own to form a bigger unit. Step 5: They do so by pooling their sovereignty and retaining their identity, so the unit grows larger while the States keep their own identity.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: Priya reads that in the city of Porto Alegre in Brazil, local inhabitants take real decisions about their own city through meetings held in every sector, and that about 20,000 people join in this decision making every year. In about 75 words, and in steps, explain how the city combines decentralisation with participative democracy, and state the changes this method has brought about.

markingPoints.description: A parallel organisation operates alongside the municipal council, enabling local inhabitants to take real decisions for their city
The city is divided into sectors or wards, and each sector has a meeting, like that of the gram sabha, in which anyone living in that area can participate
Any citizen can participate in the meetings that discuss issues affecting the entire city, and the budget of the city is discussed in these meetings
About 20,000 people participate in this decision making exercise every year
Money can no longer be spent only for the benefit of the colonies where rich people live; buses run to the poor colonies and builders cannot evict slum-dwellers without resettling them

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1: A parallel organisation works alongside the municipal council, so that local inhabitants take real decisions for their city. Step 2: The city is divided into sectors or wards, and each sector has a meeting, like that of the gram sabha, in which anyone living in that area can participate. Step 3: Any citizen can also join the meetings that discuss issues affecting the entire city, where the budget of the city is discussed. Step 4: About 20,000 people take part in this decision making exercise every year. Step 5: Money can no longer be spent only for the colonies where rich people live; buses run to the poor colonies and builders cannot evict slum-dwellers without resettling them.

evidence:
A city called Porto Alegre in Brazil has carried out an extraordinary experiment
in combining decentralisation with participative democracy. The city has set up
a parallel organisation operating alongside the municipal council, enabling local
inhabitants to take real decisions for their city.

In the first, the government for the entire country is responsible for a few subjects of common national interest, and governments at the level of provinces or states look after much of the day-to-day administering of their state. In the second country there is only one level of government, and the sub-units obey whatever the central government decides.

(b) The second country, where there is only one level of government or the sub-units are subordinate to the central government. (c) Both levels of government enjoy their power independent of the other, so neither is answerable to the other and neither can command it.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
Farhan's country is a federation. Some of its states want much greater freedom in running their own affairs, while others fear that too much freedom will break the country apart. A committee advises that governments at different levels should agree to some rules of power-sharing, and should also trust one another to keep to those rules. Farhan notes that a written agreement already exists between the levels, and wonders why a federation needs trust as well, and not just the agreement.

Read the case below and answer the questions that follow. (a) State the two objectives of a federal system that Farhan's situation reflects. (b) What two things should governments at different levels in a federation do? (c) Farhan already has the written agreement in place. Explain why an ideal federal system cannot do without the second thing as well.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (a) To safeguard and promote unity of the country, and at the same time to accommodate regional diversity. (b) They should agree to some rules of power-sharing, and should trust that each would abide by its part of the agreement. (c) An ideal federal system has both aspects, mutual trust and agreement to live together; an agreement that nobody trusts is not kept.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
Leela compares two federations. In both, independent States came together on their own to form a bigger unit, pooling sovereignty while retaining their identity. Yet in Leela's federation the central government handles many subjects, while in the other the states keep most of the day-to-day administering of their own areas. Students in both countries are taught that their country has two or more tiers of government. Leela thinks the answer to their question must lie in the way those tiers are arranged.

Read the case below and answer the questions that follow. (a) Describe the route by which independent States came together on their own to form a bigger unit in both countries. (b) State why the exact balance of power between the central and the state government is not the same in every federation. (c) Using the features of federalism, explain what these two very different federations still have in common.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (a) Independent States came together on their own to form a bigger unit, pooling sovereignty and retaining identity. (b) The exact balance of power varies from one federation to another, and depends mainly on the historical context in which the federation was formed. (c) Both have two or more tiers of government, all governing the same citizens, and each tier has its own jurisdiction in legislation, taxation and administration.
